Work samples

How I write for clients and teammates: in full sentences, calm, and ready to be picked up asynchronously.

Email: a payslip difference

Illustrative scenario. No real client details.

Client wrote: “One of our employees says her net pay is lower than last month. Can you explain why?”

Hi Amara, thanks for flagging this. A change in net pay needs a clear answer, so I have started on it now.

What I checked: this month’s payslip against last month’s, line by line.

What I found: the gap is on the deductions line, not on gross pay. I have attached both payslips with the line marked.

What happens next: I am passing it to a payroll specialist with the evidence, so you do not need to resend anything.

When you will hear from me: by 15:00 Coordinated Universal Time tomorrow, even if the update is “still checking”.

Email: an upset business client

Illustrative scenario. No real client details.

Client wrote: “Our transfer has been pending for two days and our supplier is waiting. This is unacceptable.”

Hello Mr Bello, I am sorry for the delay. It is affecting your supplier, and fixing it is our job. I have traced the transfer and escalated it as a priority with the transaction reference attached.

You will have a written update from me by 14:00 today, and I will stay on the case until it is settled. You do not need to chase us.

Asynchronous handoff note

Illustrative scenario. How I leave a case for the next shift.

Case: payslip difference · Status: escalated to payroll specialist

Done: compared both payslips and confirmed the gap is on the deductions line.

Needed: specialist to confirm the deduction rule for the client’s region.

Client told: update by 15:00 Coordinated Universal Time Thursday. Next owner: the Saturday–Wednesday shift picks up at 09:00 Coordinated Universal Time.

Pattern: third deduction question this week. Suggest a short explainer in the help docs.

How I handle a client issue

The same four steps whether it is a banking complaint or a payroll discrepancy.

  1. Gather the factsCollect the details I need from the client, the available tools and the documentation.
  2. Diagnose accuratelyPinpoint the cause before promising a fix, and check it against the process.
  3. Resolve or escalateFix it within the SLA, or hand it to a senior colleague through the defined workflow.
  4. Update and documentTell the client in clear written terms what happens next, so nobody has to wait for a call, and record the case so any teammate can pick it up asynchronously.
